BUMPED to 1.0.1 from 1.0.0. THE TRANSCRIPTION AND THE SECTION MODEL ARE UNCHANGED: source.txt is byte-identical to 1.0.0's (sha256 949790929d1913d6d958c121fafdfe1aa05b579964cbe63e0fccedd7c9450680), base.json is CARRIED unchanged, and no find and no reading of any rule moves — not one byte of the served reading view or of /plain changes. What changes is the SCOPE RECORD of this edition's ONE unscoped multi-fire rule.

THE READING-VIEW-FOLD GATE (tools/fold-probe.mjs, added at 1.0.7 of the Theology of Plato) reported this edition's r0024 as an unscoped multi-fire rule — a rule whose reading-view find fires more than once with no licence on it — and PINNED the count (1) as "reported, not fixed: a separate version and DOI are a separate decision". The decision has been taken, and the rule is now ADJUDICATED ON MEASUREMENT rather than by shape:

  r0024  "imparticipate" -> "imparticipable", 2 sites: licensed scope "all". The print sets this rule's OWN reading at BOTH sites, and sets the find form NOWHERE.

MEASURED, three ways. (1) The find occurs ONCE in source.txt; the second occurrence is the extractor's own line-join of the transcription's "imparti¬ / cipate". (2) The human-proofread witness of this same print (Project Gutenberg 78800, Distributed Proofreaders, which carries the Elements over printed pp. 301-441) reads "imparticipate" 0 times in its whole 1,305,107 bytes and "imparticipable" 84 times, 74 of them inside the Elements. (3) BLIND two-reader page reads of the TWO sites' own leaves — the two readers this library measured as non-echoing (google/gemini-2.5-flash and anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 on 10.0.0.1:8322), each given only "transcribe this page verbatim", the expected form NEVER named — read printed p. 338 "and the third as an imparti-" / "cipable." and printed p. 427 "For imparticipable life and imparticipable essence are prior to soul."

THE BRIEF'S HYPOTHESIS FOR THIS RULE IS REFUTED. It was flagged as delicate on the ground that "imparticipate" is a real word of this translation's own vocabulary, so a blanket rewrite might be a MODERNISATION of the print rather than the repair of a misprint. The print does not set it anywhere, and both of this rule's sites are the print's own "imparticipable" — one of them broken at a line end. The rule is a repair at every occurrence.

Every rule still fires and its stored `fires` is unchanged. 1.0.0 is untouched and keeps its own DOI.
